classification.summary: Carl M. Kadie of the Electronic Frontier Foundation shares a draft computer policy from the American Library Association. The post encourages those interested in the intersection of computer services and intellectual freedom to review the document.
classification.title: American Library Association Draft Computer Policy

identity.subject: American Library Association Draft Computer Policy

notable_claims: Users have the right to be free of unreasonable limitations set by system administrators, vendors, and network service providers.
Electronic communications and files should be treated as if they were public because security is technically difficult to achieve.
Libraries should not limit access to electronic resources based on controversial content or personal beliefs.
classification.summary: This item shares a draft interpretation of the Library Bill of Rights created by the ALA Intellectual Freedom Committee. The document seeks to apply traditional tenets of intellectual freedom to electronic information, emphasizing user privacy, equitable access, and protection against unreasonable limitations imposed by system administrators or vendors.
classification.title: Draft Interpretation on Access to Information, Services and Networks
